title: Find your way around
brief: After you sign in you land on the Dashboard. Everything else is reached from the side menu, and the menu shows only what your roles allow.
useCases: You just received your login and want to know where things are.
You cannot see a page a colleague mentions: your roles do not include it, ask an admin.
You want to know what is waiting for your approval.

shots.caption: The Dashboard and the side menu

steps.text: The side menu is your map. Click a group such as Treasury to open it, then pick a page.
The bell lists approvals waiting for you first, then what happened on your requests.
Your name and roles live here. Click the card to open your profile.
The Dashboard is a coming-soon page for now. Use the menu to do your work.
Click the camera to change your photo. It shows in the sidebar and the top bar.
These tiles count your roles, permissions and the approvals waiting for you.
Items whose approval step is yours are listed here, each with a Review button.
Keep your job title, phone and about text up to date here.
Demo only: "Acting as" lets you try the app as another person.

tips: Your permissions are the sum of all your roles.
Pages you cannot open send you back to the Dashboard.
The Help guides are written per role; pick yours on the Help page.

title: How approvals work
brief: Fund requests, expenses and vendor invoices are approved in steps. Which steps depends on the amount, and each step belongs to a role.
useCases: You submitted something and want to know who must approve it next.
You are an approver and want to find what is waiting for you.
An admin wants to see how the steps are set up.

steps.text: Everything whose current step is yours appears here. Click Review to open it.
"Where you approve" shows the branches of the approval tree where one of your roles is a step.

shots.caption: The approval flow of a request

steps.text: Each step shows its role and who approved it. The step with a yellow number is waiting.
Only someone with the step's role can approve at that step. Others see who it is waiting for.

tips: Small amounts need one approval; bigger ones need more. Admins edit the tree in Configuration > Roles and permissions.
A request keeps the path it had when it was submitted.
The last approval finishes it; a rejection at any step stops it, with a reason.

title: Ask for money (fund request)
brief: A fund request asks the company for money for a purpose. It is approved by the approval tree and then paid by Accounts. You can follow every step.
useCases: You need cash for a site visit, materials or an event.
You want to know if your request was approved and how much you received.
You want to correct or cancel a request that is still waiting.

steps.text: Your wallet shows what you received from funds, month by month.
Click Request Funds to ask for money.
Your requests are listed with their status. Click one to see its details.
Enter the amount you need.
Say what the money is for, so approvers can decide quickly.
Add the work order if the money is for a project.
Submit. The request goes to the first approver.

tips: A request has no category, branch or department. When Accounts pay it, the money goes to your wallet.
You can edit or cancel a request while it is still pending.

title: Approve and pay a fund request
brief: Approvers pass or reject a request step by step. Once it is approved, Accounts pay it from a fund of the right category, in one or several payments.
useCases: A request is waiting for your step in the approval tree.
Accounts need to pay an approved request.
A request is rejected because the cost is already covered.

steps.text: Check the amount, purpose and requester.
The approval flow shows which step is yours.
Approve (you set the approved amount) or reject with a reason.
Choose the fund category first, then the fund the money comes from.
The amount cannot be more than what is still approved or what the fund has.
Confirm. The fund balance drops and a transaction is recorded.

tips: A request can be paid in parts; its status shows Partially paid until the approved amount is paid.
Only people with the Pay permission see Record Payment.

title: Return unused money or close a request
brief: If you received more than you spent, give it back so Accounts can take it into a fund. If only part of an approved amount was paid and the rest is not needed, close the request.
useCases: You spent less than you received.
The job was cancelled after a part payment.
Accounts want to confirm money they received back.

steps.text: Return funds: enter the amount you are giving back and how.
Close request: the unpaid rest of the approved amount is released.
Returns appear in the request details until Accounts confirm them.
A return waits here for confirmation.
Confirm received into a fund, or reject with a reason.

tips: A return only counts once Accounts confirm it.
Employees return only what they received and have not returned yet.

title: Organization funds
brief: Organization Funds shows the company's cash, bank and other funds: balance, reserved money, minimum balance and recent activity.
useCases: You want to know how much money is available and where.
A fund is running low and needs a top-up.
You need to add a new bank or cash fund.

steps.text: Tiles show balance, available and reserved money.
Click a category to filter the funds and the chart.
Add a new fund with the add button.
Download or share the activity as Excel or PDF.

tips: Funds are grouped by categories managed in Configuration > Categories.
A fund below its minimum balance is flagged.

title: Transactions, returns and reports
brief: Transactions is the record of every payment, return and action on fund requests. Employees see only their own; Accounts and admins see all.
useCases: You need a statement for a date range.
You want to send a report as an online link.
An admin wants to see every treasury movement.

steps.text: Tabs: payments, returns, actions and (admins) treasury movements.
Choose the dates you need.
Download Excel or PDF, or create a share link.

tips: Share links open only in the browser that created them until the app has a server.

title: Enter an expense in seconds
brief: Quick entry saves a cost with just a date, category, amount and a few words. Press Enter and the next one is ready.
useCases: You have a pile of small bills to record.
A cost is small and needs no extra details.
You want to see everything you entered.

steps.text: Pick the date (today is filled in).
Choose the category; the type of category decides what details exist in the full form.
Type the amount.
Say what it was for, then press Enter to save.
steps.target: form[aria-label="Quick entry"] input[placeholder="What was it for?"]

steps.text: Where the money goes: click a bar to filter the list by that category.

fill: form[aria-label="Quick entry"] input[placeholder="What was it for?"]

press: form[aria-label="Quick entry"] input[placeholder="What was it for?"]

steps.text: A green message confirms the number of the new expense.
The entry appears in the list. Small amounts are approved automatically.

tips: Up to the no-approval limit an expense is approved when you save it; larger ones go to approval.
Need receipts or items? Use Add expense for the full form.

title: Enter a purchase with items and receipts
brief: The full form asks for the details that belong to the category: items for a purchase, route for transport, month for rent. You can attach receipt photos.
useCases: You bought goods and want the items and prices recorded.
You paid a vendor and want it linked to what you owe them.
A cost belongs to a project.

steps.text: Choose the category first. It decides which fields appear.
Add the items bought. The amount is the sum of the lines.
The form shows the last, lowest and average price paid, and warns if your price is higher.
steps.target: [role=dialog] [aria-label="Price history of Copper lug 120 sq mm"]

steps.text: Link the expense to a project so it counts in the project costing.
Attach photos of the bill or receipt.

tips: Items not in the product list are added to it once the expense is approved.
You can edit or delete your own expense while it waits for approval or after a rejection.

title: Approve and pay expenses
brief: Larger expenses wait for approval. Approved ones are paid by someone with the Pay permission, optionally taking the money from a fund.
useCases: An expense above the no-approval limit needs your step.
Accounts pay an approved expense from a fund.
A payment to a vendor should reduce what is owed to that vendor.

steps.text: Check the details and the receipts.
The flow shows who approves next.
Approve your step, or reject with a reason.
Choose the fund to pay from, or leave it as record only.
Pick the method and date; add a cheque or transaction number.
Confirm. A payment to a vendor also lowers what you owe them.

tips: A vendor payment cannot be more than what is due to the vendor.
A paid expense stays on record and cannot be deleted.

title: Manage expense categories
brief: Expense categories live in Configuration > Categories. Each has a type that decides which details the expense form asks for.
useCases: You need a new kind of cost such as Warranty claims.
You want to rename a category.
A purchase category should ask for items.

steps.text: Use the chips to jump to a section.
Name the new category.
Choose its type: purchase of goods, vendor payment, transport, food, rent, promotion or general.
Edit or delete a category. One that has expenses cannot be deleted.

tips: Renames show everywhere at once.
The type of a category cannot change once expenses use it.

title: From a purchase to stock to a project
brief: Goods you buy are entered as an expense with items, approved, then received into a store. When they are issued to a project, their cost reaches the project costing.
useCases: You bought cable lugs and want them in the store.
You want the project to pay for the lugs only when they are used.
You want to avoid typing the same product twice.

steps.text: Choose where the items come from: an expense, a vendor order, or by hand.
Pick the approved purchase; its items and prices fill in.
Check quantities and costs, then save.

tips: Expenses that went into stock are not counted in the project cost when bought; they count when issued.
Item names are matched with the product list ignoring capitals.

title: Receive, issue, transfer and count stock
brief: Each store keeps its own stock, worked out from every movement. You can receive, issue to a project, transfer between stores and correct counts.
useCases: Goods arrive at the office store.
Material goes to a site: issue it to the project or transfer it to the project store.
A physical count differs from the system.

steps.text: Choose a store: office stores and project stores.
These buttons are the stock actions you are allowed to use.
Low stock is flagged against the minimum set on the product.
Tabs: the catalogue, every movement, and purchases.
Pick the product. Assets cannot be issued; transfer them instead.
You cannot issue more than is in stock.
Charge it to a project; its cost then counts in the project costing.

tips: Value uses the running average cost of the store.
Cost columns need the View cost permission.

title: See what you paid before
brief: Price history lists every price paid for a product, from expenses, vendor orders and hand receipts, with the lowest, highest and average.
useCases: You buy the same item often at different prices.
You want to know which supplier is cheapest.
You want to spot a price that suddenly jumped.

steps.text: The last price is shown with the change since the previous price.
Click a price to open its history.

actions.click: button[aria-label="Price history of Copper lug 120 sq mm"]

steps.text: Last, average, lowest and highest price at a glance.
The line shows how the price moved; hover a dot for the supplier.
Every purchase with its supplier and where it was recorded.
Vendors' current price lists, cheapest first.

tips: Prices are matched by item name; keep names consistent.
The expense form shows the same hint while you type.

title: Work with vendors
brief: Vendors are suppliers (products), service providers or others. For each you can send purchase orders, approve invoices, pay, and give them a login.
useCases: A new supplier needs to be set up.
You are ordering goods for a project.
A vendor sent an invoice to approve and pay.

steps.text: Click a type to filter: product, service or other.
Add a vendor with its type and details.
The columns show invoiced, paid and due at a glance.
Pick items from the vendor's product list; the price fills in.
Link the order to a project if it is bought for one.
Send the order.
The chips show the approval steps for the invoice amount.
Open the photo of the invoice.
Approve your step or reject with a reason.

tips: Approved invoices raise the amount due. Payments lower it.
A vendor with orders, invoices or payments cannot be deleted; mark it inactive.

title: Vendor login: invoices and due payments
brief: As a vendor you see only your own orders, invoices and payments. You can submit invoices with a photo and ask for part of what is due.
useCases: You delivered goods and want to get paid.
You want to know how much is due and what was already paid.
You want to ask for a part payment this week.

steps.text: These tiles show total invoiced, paid, due now and requested.
Tabs: your products, purchase orders, invoices, payments and history.
Enter the invoice number and amount.
Link the purchase order it belongs to.
Add a photo or scan of the invoice (an image, up to 2 MB).
You can ask for up to the amount that is due and not yet requested.
Staff accept or decline; you see their answer here.

tips: Your invoice is approved in steps; you can see its status.
You cannot see other vendors or any company-only pages.

title: Work with clients and their documents
brief: A client record holds company details, documents (requirements, purchase orders, work orders, bills, delivery challans) and the logins that follow the client's projects.
useCases: A new client signed a work order.
You received a purchase order and need to file it.
You want to send a bill by link or email.

steps.text: Search by name, contact or city.
Add a client.
Open a client to see everything about it.
Filter by document type.
Add a document; both staff and the client can send documents.
Share a document as a read-only link or by email.
Link an existing user, or create a new client login.
A client login sees only its own client and projects.

tips: Share links open only in the browser that created them until there is a server.
Projects are managed in Projects; the client page shows them read-only.

title: Client login: follow your projects
brief: As a client you see your own projects with progress and updates, and the documents exchanged. You can send requirements, purchase orders and other documents.
useCases: You want to know how far a project is.
You need to send a purchase order or requirement.
You want to find a bill or delivery challan.

steps.text: Each project shows its status, progress and dates.
Updates posted by the project manager are listed under each project.
Choose the type: requirement, purchase order, work order, bill or delivery challan.
Give a title and, if needed, the amount and a file.
Save. Encore staff can see it right away.

tips: You can delete only documents you sent.
You cannot see other clients.

title: Projects, costing and profit
brief: A project ties a client's contract to its budget, team and costs. Cost and profit are worked out automatically from expenses, vendor invoices and store issues.
useCases: A client signed a contract and you need to track cost against it.
You want to know if a project is making money.
You need to assign a manager and set payment terms.

steps.text: Tiles total the contracts, budgets and profit.
Create a project: choose the client, type, manager, branch, budget and payment terms.
Cost and profit per project at a glance.
Cost to date, earned from progress, profit to date and projected profit.
Budget used and where the cost comes from.
Every cost line with its source: expense, vendor purchase or store issue.

tips: Goods bought into a store count when issued to the project, never twice.
Projects are visible to managers who run them, and to clients without costs.

title: Roles and permissions
brief: Roles decide what each person can do. A person can have several roles and gets the sum of their permissions.
useCases: A new job needs its own role.
A role should stop being able to delete things.
A person needs two roles at once.

steps.text: Create a role with a name and description.
Admin is built in and always has everything.
Tick what each role may do.
Tick a whole group at once with its first row.
Tick every role the person needs.
Someone active must always keep a role that can assign roles.

tips: Roles in use cannot be deleted.
New permissions appear for all roles as features are added.

title: Set up the approval tree
brief: The approval tree says who approves what, by amount. Bigger amounts add steps.
useCases: Large expenses should also need the Admin.
A new approver role must be added to a branch.
You want to test which path an amount takes.

steps.text: Each branch shows the amounts it covers and its steps in order.
Add a branch for larger amounts.
steps.target: button:has-text("Add a branch for larger amounts")

steps.text: Try an amount to see its path.

tips: A request keeps the path it had when submitted.
The first branch always starts at zero.

title: Employees, admins and logins
brief: The Users menu manages people: employees (HR details, salary, promotions), admins, and logins for vendors, clients and customers.
useCases: A new employee joined.
Someone was promoted and their salary changed.
A vendor contact needs a login.

steps.text: Add an employee: profile, work, salary and access are separate tabs.
Filter by department and employment type.
Open the actions menu for edit, financial records, promotion and delete.
Edit the details.
Financial records and promotion need the matching permissions.
Make someone an admin; someone active must always stay an admin.
Vendor, client and customer logins are managed on their own pages under Users.

tips: Salary details need the View salary permission.
An employee name used on fund requests cannot be changed.

title: Change the look of the app
brief: Theme changes colours, logo, page background, sidebar and table design for everyone. Changes preview live and stay only after you save.
useCases: The company logo or colours changed.
Tables are too crowded and need more air.
You want the sidebar glass wallpaper changed.

steps.text: Start from a preset, then adjust.
Upload the company logo and choose colours.
Save to keep the changes for everyone, or discard.

tips: The browser tab icon and the E mark follow the theme colours.
Changes are only a preview until you save.

title: Customers
brief: Customers are people who buy from the company. A customer login has no company link and, for now, sees only the Dashboard and its profile.
useCases: You want to record a customer and give them a login.
You plan to give customers features later.

steps.text: Add a customer with name, email, phone and address.
Edit or delete a customer login.

tips: Give the Customer role permissions in Roles and permissions when customer features arrive.

title: Financial records of an employee
brief: Open an employee's financial records to see everything between the company and the person over their whole time: pay, bonuses, fund deposits and refunds, fund request money and promotions. Download it as Excel or PDF, or share a link.
useCases: Accounts need a statement for one person.
An employee asks how much is in their security or provident fund.
You are refunding part of a fund balance.
You want to see what an employee still owes from fund requests.

steps.text: Four numbers: lifetime earnings, held in funds, taken on fund requests, still to settle.
Download or share the whole statement as Excel or PDF.
Switch between Overview, Transactions and Funds.
Narrow the list by type, or search it.
Totals of what is listed: received, returned, kept in funds.
Each line shows the type, details, date and who recorded it. Green is money received, red returned, blue kept in a fund. Scroll down to see them.
Balance and total withdrawn of each fund.
Type an amount and press Refund balance to pay part of it back. You cannot refund more than the balance.

tips: Downloading needs the Export permission under Users; the drawer needs View salary.
The download always has the whole lifetime, whatever the list is filtered to.
A refund is recorded in the list at once.

title: Companies, branches, departments, teams, warehouses
brief: Configuration > Company defines how the organisation is built: companies, then branches, departments and teams, plus the warehouses (stores) of each branch. Employees and expenses are placed on this structure so costs can be seen per branch and department.
useCases: A new branch or department opens.
You want to see what each branch or department spent.
A warehouse needs a manager or a different branch.
You add a second company.

steps.text: Each card shows branches, departments, warehouses and people.
Add another company with its legal and contact details.
The tree shows branch, department and team with the people in each.
Add a branch here; select any unit to add under it.
Select a unit to see its head, people and actions: add, edit, deactivate, delete.
Choose the period.
Approved expenses, per branch with its departments under it.

tips: A unit with children, people or warehouses cannot be deleted; deactivate it instead.
Warehouses are the stores of the Store feature, placed under a branch.
Place employees in Users > Employees > Work. Charge expenses on the expense and fund request forms.
Costs need the View costs permission under Company.
